title: Audible Is Less Than $1/Month for 3 Months With This Fall Audiobook Deal
description: Audible has rolled out one of its steepest subscription discounts of the year ahead of Black Friday, bringing the price of its audiobook service dow
body:
Audible has rolled out one of its steepest subscription discounts of the year ahead of Black Friday, bringing the price of its audiobook service down to less than a dollar a month.

	From now through Dec. 28, eligible subscribers can sign up for three months of Audible Standard for just 99 cents per month, down from its usual $8.99 monthly price. As part of the holiday promotion, subscribers will also receive a $20 Audible credit to put toward additional audiobook purchases.


	The Amazon-owned platform’s Standard membership allows subscribers to choose one audiobook per month from its catalog of more than one million titles, in addition to unlimited podcast listening. The monthly audiobook selections remain accessible for the duration of one’s membership. Once the promotional period ends, the subscription automatically renews at $8.99 per month, although members can cancel at any time.

	For more voracious readers, Audible’s $14.95-per-month Premium membership offers unlimited listening to a rotating library of more than 150,000 audiobooks and Audible Originals, in addition to one monthly audiobook credit that can be redeemed for any title in its broader catalog. Unlike Standard members’ monthly selections, audiobooks purchased with Premium credits are yours to keep even after canceling your subscription.

	You can check out Audible’s complete catalogue here, which includes celebrity memoirs like Lena Dunham’s “Famesick,” Britney Spears’ “The Woman in Me,” Al Pacino’s “Sonny Boy” and Viola Davis’s “Finding Me,” in addition to book-to-screen adaptations such as “It Ends With Us,” “The Perfect Couple,” and “Uglies.” Check out some of the year’s buzziest releases here.


	Sign up for Audible’s Black Friday deal through Dec. 28.

schema.headline: Audible Is Less Than $1/Month for 3 Months With This Fall Audiobook Deal

title: Kevin Kline Reunites With Meryl Streep in ‘The Corrections’ Series at Netflix
description:
Kevin Kline will star opposite Meryl Streep in the Netflix limited series adaptation of “The Corrections,” Variety has learned. 

	Based on the nov
body:
Kevin Kline will star opposite Meryl Streep in the Netflix limited series adaptation of “The Corrections,” Variety has learned. 

	Based on the novel of the same name by Jonathan Franzen, the series was originally announced with Streep attached back in April. 

	The logline describes the show as “a sharply comic portrait of a Midwestern family whose three unmoored adult siblings desperately resist their mother’s (Streep) wish for one last Christmas together – each undone by the delusional ambitions that were supposed to save them from becoming their parents.”
	

	Kline will star as Alfred Lambert, who is described as “a once-powerful patriarch who is battling the afflictions of aging. A man of strict principles and old-fashioned decorum, Alfred must come to terms with his three very modern children—a daughter whose secrets he can no longer protect, an older son who has displaced him as the authority in the family, and a wayward son whose forgiveness he yearns for.” 

	The casting marks the latest collaboration between Kline and Streep. The two most famously worked together in the hit 1982 drama “Sophie’s Choice,” which was Kline’s feature debut and for which Streep earned her second Academy Award. Kline and Streep have also appeared onscreen together in the films “A Prairie Home Companion” and “Ricki and the Flash.” 

	Kline is primarily known for his film roles, but has been in a number of shows in recent years. He has lent his voice to the hit Fox animated series “Bob’s Burgers” since the show began, while he also recently starred in the shows “American Classic” for MGM+ and “Disclaimer” at Apple TV. In film, Kline won the Academy Award for best supporting actor for his work in “A Fish Called Wanda.” Along with the projects he has done with Streep, he has starred in features including “The Big Chill,” “Silverado,” “Cry Freedom,” “French Kiss,” and “In & Out.” 
	

	He is repped by UTA and Berwick & Kovacik. 

	Franzen will adapt his novel for the screen and executive produce, with Streep executive producing in addition to starring. Mark Roybal and Paul Lee executive produce for wiip, with Nicole Clemens and Amy Sayres executive producing as well. Cord Jefferson will executive produce and direct all episodes. Paramount Television Studios (soon to be Warner Bros. Television Studios) will produce.

schema.headline: Kevin Kline Reunites With Meryl Streep in ‘The Corrections’ Series at Netflix

title: ‘Aquamarine’ TV Series Greenlit at Disney+, Disney Channel
description:
Disney has officially picked up the series adaptation of “Aquamarine,” Variety has learned. 

	The live-action series will air on both Disney Chann
body:
Disney has officially picked up the series adaptation of “Aquamarine,” Variety has learned. 

	The live-action series will air on both Disney Channel and Disney+. It was originally announced with a pilot order back in June. 

	The series stars Kenzi Richardson, Briella Guiza, Theodore Dalton, and Annika Reese. Emma Roberts and Jake McDorman, who both starred in the original 2006 film, will reprise their roles in the series. 


	“‘Aquamarine’ is a timeless coming-of-age story, and we’re excited to bring its humor, heart and sense of wonder to a new generation,” said Ayo Davis, president of Disney Kids & Family. “At its core, it’s a story about the power of friendship, self-discovery and believing in yourself. And with a stellar cast led by Kenzi Richardson, there’s a magical quality to this story that I think audiences everywhere will really connect with.” 
	

	The logline for the show states, “When teenager Coral (Richardson) moves to a dreamy seaside town, she begins unraveling the truth behind her mother’s disappearance — and discovers her mother is a mermaid, awakening magical powers in Coral just as secrets beneath the waves threaten to surface.” 

	The project hails from writer and executive producer Sarah Watson (“The Bold Type”), with the film’s director, Elizabeth Allen Rosenbaum, directing the pilot and executive producing. Susan Cartsonis, who produced the film, also executive produces. Both Roberts and McDorman are executive producers on the series. John Quaintance and Jessica Bendinger wrote the original film, which was based on a novel of the same name by Alice Hoffman. Quintance, Bendinger, and Hoffman are not involved in the series.
	

	Along with Roberts and McDorman, “Aquamarine” starred Joanna “JoJo” Levesque, Sara Paxton, and Arielle Kebbel. In the film, best friends Claire (Roberts) and Hailey (Levesque) try to help mermaid Aquamarine (Paxton) find true love. The film was not particularly well-received when it was first released, but has since achieved cult status.

schema.headline: ‘Aquamarine’ TV Series Greenlit at Disney+, Disney Channel

title: John Turturro, Carrie Coon, Guitarricadelafuente and Peter Gamble Among SFFILM Awards Night Honorees
description: John Turturro, Carrie Coon, Guitarricadelafuente and Peter Gamble are the SFFILM awards night honorees for 2026. The ceremony will take place Dec.
body:
John Turturro, Carrie Coon, Guitarricadelafuente and Peter Gamble are the SFFILM awards night honorees for 2026. The ceremony will take place Dec. 7 at San Francisco’s Gateway Pavilion at Fort Mason Center for Arts & Culture.

	“Carrie, Guitarricadelafuente, Peter and John each bring a distinct sensibility and an uncommon command of their craft to the screen this season,” Jessie Fairbanks, SFFILM’s director of programming, said in a statement. “We selected this group because they represent the range of talent and creative perspectives that make cinema so compelling, and their work speaks to the thoughtful, nuanced and often unexpected films that make a season memorable. They bring a fearlessness, determination and depth of perspective that we are proud to celebrate at SFFILM.”
	

	The recognition aims to highlight four distinguished artists who continue to shape contemporary cinema. 

	Turturro, currently appearing in “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York,” will receive the Maria Manetti Shrem Award for Acting. Past recipients include Benicio Del Toro, Demi Moore, Nicolas Cage, Margot Robbie, Glenn Close, Adam Driver and Amy Adams.

	Coon will be honored with the Katie & Todd Traina Award for Acting. She is the inaugural recipient of this award for her performance in Guy Nattiv’s psychological thriller “The Liberation.”

	“La Bola Negra” star Guitarricadelafuente will receive the SFFILM Award for Virtuosity. Past recipients include Wunmi Mosaku, director Malcolm Washington, Cord Jefferson and Stephanie Hsu. His award will be presented by “La Bola Negra” directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi.
	

	Presented by “I Play Rocky” star Anthony Ippolito, the film’s screenwriter Gamble will take home the Nion McEvoy & Leslie Berriman Award for Storytelling. Past honorees include Kristen Stewart, Jason Reitman, Roger Ross Williams, Sarah Polley, Maggie Gyllenhaal, Aaron Sorkin, Lulu Wang, Boots Riley, Emily V. Gordon and Kumail Nanjiani.

	SFFILM Awards Night aims to bring together the film industry’s most influential talent for an evening that celebrates cinema and fuels the next generation of storytellers by raising funds for the organization.

schema.headline: John Turturro, Carrie Coon, Guitarricadelafuente and Peter Gamble Among SFFILM Awards Night Honorees

title: ‘Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power’ Renewed for Season 4 at Amazon Prime Video
description:
“The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power” has been renewed for Season 4 at Amazon Prime Video.

	The Tolkien series, which is set thousands of ye
body:
“The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power” has been renewed for Season 4 at Amazon Prime Video.

	The Tolkien series, which is set thousands of years before the books in Middle-earth, is in pre-production for the new season and will begin filming in spring 2027 at Shepperton Studios in the U.K.

	The renewal comes on the day the final two episodes of Season 3 are airing on Amazon Prime Video.


	“‘The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power’ has become a defining series for Prime Video,” said Peter Friedlander, Head of Global Television, Amazon MGM Studios. “As Season 3 delivers the landmark moment fans have been waiting for — the forging of the One Ring — we are proud to confirm Season 4 with J.D. Payne, Patrick McKay, and the entire creative team. We look forward to bringing fans even deeper into the rich world of Tolkien’s Second Age.”
	

	“The Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power” stars Cynthia Addai-Robinson, Robert Aramayo, Owain Arthur, Maxim Baldry, Jamie Campbell Bower, Morfydd Clark, Ismael Cruz Córdova, Charles Edwards, Trystan Gravelle, Ciarán Hinds, Tyroe Muhafidin, Sophia Nomvete, Lloyd Owen, Andrew Richardson, Charlie Vickers, Benjamin Walker and Daniel Weyman.

	The third season of “The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power” was produced by showrunners and executive producers J.D. Payne and Patrick McKay, who are joined by executive producers Lindsey Weber, Kate Hazell, Justin Doble and Charlotte Brändström, who also directs. Matthew Penry-Davey is a producer and Ally O’Leary Cantrell, Tim Keene, and Andrew Lee are co-producers.

schema.headline: ‘Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power’ Renewed for Season 4 at Amazon Prime Video

title: Elizabeth Holmes’ Ex-Assistant Speaks Out on ‘You Can See Everything’ and Amanda Seyfried’s ‘Valid’ Performance: Holmes ‘Softened a Lot in the Film’
description:
For Aria Marinelli, “You Can See Everything” hit a little close to home.

	Marinelli, who worked as Elizabeth Holmes’ assistant in 2009, during the
body:
For Aria Marinelli, “You Can See Everything” hit a little close to home.

	Marinelli, who worked as Elizabeth Holmes’ assistant in 2009, during the early stages of Theranos, spoke about watching her former boss in the documentary in an interview with Warner Bailey on “AvA Live.”

	“My initial reaction was I did not want to see it,” Marinelli said of the Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim film. But then, eventually, “I acquiesced and went out of sheer morbid curiosity, and I came out of there just feeling really contemplative. I mean, she’s a real human that I interacted with, and to see her up there going to jail with children was really emotionally charged for me, as someone who does have a kid as well.”
	

	When “You Can See Everything” surprise premiered at Telluride and became one of the buzziest films of the year, Marinelli, who has rarely spoken about her time at Theranos 17 years ago, realized, “I have a voice in this too. [Holmes] doesn’t get to be the one to just come back on the scene and control the narrative.”

	Marinelli called the film a “crazy, wonderful, thoughtful, strategic piece,” and praised Fielder’s ability to portray Holmes as she truly is. “I do think he’s done it justice.”

	Compared to her time running the fraudulent blood-testing startup, “She seems like she’s softened a lot in the film,” Marinelli said of Holmes. “But she still seems like she really wants to win.”



	

									Courtesy of AvA
	



	Amanda Seyfried plays a big part in “You Can See Everything,” reprising her role as Holmes in reenactments with Fielder after the Theranos founder went to prison. One of the tension points in the three-hour A24 film is Seyfried’s portrayal of Holmes in the hit Hulu miniseries “The Dropout.” Billy Evans, Holmes’ romantic partner, clashes with Seyfried in the movie as he accuses her (and everyone else who worked on the series) of peddling lies about Holmes for the sake of entertainment.
	

	Marinelli, who knew Holmes intimately in 2009, said watching “The Dropout” was “remarkable” because “I can vouch for a lot of that.” (As an example: “I remember she listened to rap music really loud.”)

	Asked if she thought Seyfried’s depiction of Holmes was “fair,” Marinelli said, “Yeah, I do, because a lot of the things I saw were measured and valid. Obviously they’re dramatized, because it needs to keep people’s interest. But there was nothing I saw that seemed out of sorts with what I knew to be true.”

	Holmes is currently serving a 10-year prison sentence and is expected to be released in 2030. In the film, she and Evans tell Fielder they are working on a new biotech startup, continuing the progress of Theranos.

	As to whether Holmes deserves a second chance, Marinelli said, “I think people are complex, and we always deserve second chances. It might not be the best idea to go into the same field where you’ve already burned all the bridges, very publicly. It’s a complex question, and not for me to answer, because she needs to decide the direction her life takes after something like that. I can’t imagine what it must feel like to reset, especially if she truly believes she was following her dream. But yeah, I think we all deserve a second chance.”

	Bailey is the founder of Assistants vs. Agents, a digital media startup geared toward Hollywood’s labor class. On “AvA Live,” he interviews entertainment industry insiders and former assistants sharing advice for the next generation of leaders. Marinelli now works as the vice president of fan experience strategy at Arena One.

	Watch Marinelli’s full interview on “AvA Live” below.

title: Benjamín Naishtat’s ‘The Seven Madmen,’ With ‘I’m Still Here’ Star Selton Mello, Wraps Production
description: “The Seven Madmen,” starring Selton Mello (“I’m Still Here”) and directed by Benjamín Naishtat, is wrapping its shoot in Buenos Aires on Nov. 24, m
body:
“The Seven Madmen,” starring Selton Mello (“I’m Still Here”) and directed by Benjamín Naishtat, is wrapping its shoot in Buenos Aires on Nov. 24, marking the latest advance on a production that weighs in as one of Latin America’s big bets for A-List festival selection in 2027.

	A present day noir thriller loosely adapting Argentinean novelist Robert Arlt’s 1929 and 1931 modern classic novels “The Seven Madmen” and “The Flamethrowers,” the movie also reps the latest feature from Argentina’s Naishtat (“Rojo,” “Puan,” “Glaxo”) who is fast consolidating as one of Latin America’s major auteurs.
	

	Naishtat also forms part of a loose knit but burgeoning new generation of Spanish-language cineastes (think Spain’s Rodrigo Sorogoyen) that have a clear sense of film genre and combine bold visuals with a large concern for contemporary social issues.

	“The Seven Madmen” also stars Martin Piroyansky (“Porno y helado”). Arlt’s novel of the same time turned on young Remo Erdosian who’s threatened with imprisonment unless he returns money he’s stolen. He seeks out Alberto, a mysterious Astrologer, who promises to help Remo if in return the young man joins his organization which, he discovers, aims to overthrow the government.

	Just how much of that get into Naishtat’s film, given it is also inspired by “The Flamethrowers,” remains to be seen with its producers keeping its plot under wraps, describing it as “set in a twisted Buenos Aires” and “an intense thriller.” It is known, however, that Piroyansky plays Remo and Mello the Astrologer.
	

	“Benjamín is a deeply inspiring filmmaker,” Mello told Variety. “It is an honor to have been invited by him to bring to life one of the most iconic characters in Argentine literature: El Astrólogo, created by Roberto Arlt and now reimagined by Benjamín in the film we are making together.”

	Mello added: “I have been experiencing something new: a sense of Latin American belonging that moves me deeply while also expanding my artistic expression. This project has brought about an intimate celebration of a rare and very special moment in my journey.”

	Cast is rounded up by Lorena Vega (“Envious”), Diego Cremonesi, Sofía Morandi, Andrea Frigerio, Iván González, Paula Grinszpan and Lola Berthet, with Carla Peterson (“27 Nights”) and special guest star Mercedes Morán (“The Kingdom”).

	“Ever since I first read ‘The Seven Madmen,’ I have been captivated by its dark beauty, by its characters who exist beyond the reach of any law, and by its ability to capture Buenos Aires in a way perhaps no other book ever has,” said Naishtat.

	He added that he had spent “more than 10 years” working on an adaptation which he knew was “impossible, which, in a way, came as a relief, since my interpretation is decidedly free.”

	“At the darkest moment in Argentine cinema, devastated by a government hostile to any form of cultural expression, an eclectic group of producers from around the world, an extraordinary cast, and a world-class crew joined forces to make this project a reality.”

	In an era where Latin American films of late ambition can only be made with streaming service support or multi-lateral co-production, the “eclectic group” referred to by Naishtat takes in Argentina’s Púcara Cine, founded by Federico Eibuszyc, which produced Naishtat’s “The Movement,” “Rojo” and “Puán” and Pasto, founded by Bárbara Francisco Mendivilm which teamed with Púcara to produce “Puan.”

	They are joined by “Argentina 1985” producer Infinity Hill, Particular Crowd (“The Extortion”) and Brazilian production companies MyMama Entertainment (“Medusa”) and Bubbles Project (“Elephants in the Fog,”) and Ecce Films (France), Materia Cinema (Spain), and Pandora Films (Germany), in association with Bord Cadre and Sula Films.
	

	It is no coincidence that two novels published in 1929 and 1931, an era of social fanaticism which saw the rise of fascism, are now set to receive a free present-day adaptation.

	“Revisiting the unclassifiable marvel that Roberto Arlt published in 1929 is a timely endeavor in order to decipher the Argentinian and planetary present, said Naishtat.

	Noted Particular Crowd President Peter Bevan: ”’The Seven Madmen’ pulsates with relentless tension, singular humor and Benjamín Naishtat’s signature lucidity.”



	

					Lorena Vega

schema.headline: Benjamín Naishtat’s ‘The Seven Madmen,’ With ‘I’m Still Here’ Star Selton Mello, Wraps Production

title: ‘One & Only’ Campaign: BOTOX® Cosmetic (onabotulinumtoxinA) Has Been FDA Approved for Over 20 Years
description:
Click here for Medication Guide, including Boxed Warning. 

	In a world where trends come and go, there’s one thing that never goes out of style: be
body:
Click here for Medication Guide, including Boxed Warning. 

	In a world where trends come and go, there’s one thing that never goes out of style: being authentically yourself. The “One & Only” campaign from BOTOX® Cosmetic honors exactly that by showcasing everyday people doing what they love, from work and family life to hobbies and self-expression. The campaign, which launched in mid-2025, also focuses on individuality and real patient stories to celebrate unique individualities. Real people with real motivations and real results, embracing what makes them the one and only, including Mandy Ansari Jensen.
	



	

	



	“As a new mom, balancing everything important to me can be a lot,” says the content creator and BOTOX® Cosmetic influencer partner. BOTOX® Cosmetic is FDA approved to temporarily improve the look of moderate to severe frown lines, crow’s feet, forehead lines and vertical bands connecting the neck and jaw (platysma bands) in adults. “I love doing things that prioritize self-care. A consultation for BOTOX® Cosmetic is one of those things. Every time I see my provider and get treated, I know I will still look like me, just with fewer lines.”

	The “One & Only” campaign builds on the foundation of BOTOX® Cosmetic celebrating real people and real stories. Now, “One & Only” takes that message forward by celebrating the idea of being distinct. Each story is unique. “The one & only BOTOX® Cosmetic. The one & only you,” the campaign emphasizes. 

	Treatment with BOTOX® Cosmetic can deliver natural-looking results and help make lines less noticeable. That’s the heart of the “One & Only” campaign: With BOTOX® Cosmetic, you’re still you, just with fewer lines.
	

	In two clinical trials, a majority of patients reported they were “Mostly or Very Satisfied” with their overall treatment results at day 60. In addition, these patients reported the same responses for the natural-looking result of treatment for their frown and forehead lines. In a 2022 survey, a majority of respondents treated for their crow’s feet lines said they “Completely or Somewhat Agree” that BOTOX® Cosmetic provides natural-looking results.



	

	



	“For me, life has never been about perfection. It’s about authenticity and feeling like myself,” Jensen shares. “Taking ownership over how I show up in the world makes me feel unique and true to myself. With BOTOX® Cosmetic, my provider can treat my moderate to severe frown lines, forehead lines, and crow’s feet — I am confident about my results* after getting treated and am happy with the natural-looking results BOTOX® Cosmetic provides. It’s not about changing who I am. It’s about prioritizing myself through every stage of life. I’m glad I had a consultation with my provider, who helped me understand that there are risks with this product as well. The effects of BOTOX® Cosmetic may spread hours to weeks after injection and can cause serious symptoms, so don’t forget to speak to your provider to see if it’s right for you.”

	*Based on a 2025 study of experienced neurotoxin users (n = 512) in which 263 patients had received BOTOX® Cosmetic within the last 6 months. When asked if they feel confident in their results after BOTOX® Cosmetic treatment, 95% responded “Agree/Strongly Agree.”

	BOTOX® Cosmetic is the first FDA approved product of its kind to temporarily improve the look of moderate to severe frown lines, forehead lines and crow’s feet in adults. Not only has the nonsurgical prescription treatment been FDA approved for more than two decades, but it’s also the most researched, tested and peer-reviewed treatment of its kind* — even becoming the first FDA approved neurotoxin for use beyond the face (BOTOX® Cosmetic temporarily improves the look of moderate to severe vertical bands connecting the neck and jaw).

	*Over 6,800 publications featuring BOTOX® (onabotulinumtoxinA) or BOTOX® Cosmetic.

	“The ‘One & Only’ campaign was launched to mark a new chapter for BOTOX® Cosmetic, building on our brand’s 20-year legacy as the most researched and trusted product of its kind1,*,+,” says Glen Curran, Senior Vice President of U.S., Allergan Aesthetics. “We created this campaign to highlight real people and their stories. Our goal is to empower patients to embrace the one and only version of themselves while sharing the brand’s position as the original, and the one and only, product of its kind that’s been FDA approved for over 20 years.”
	

	For decades, aesthetic treatments have been associated with Hollywood stars and global entertainers. Accessibility has changed that. Today, BOTOX® Cosmetic consumers include mothers prioritizing self-care, entrepreneurs dominating their industries, and artists owning their personal vision. “The ‘One & Only’ campaign shows real people doing what they love, demonstrating that our brand supports individuality,” says Curran. “This campaign encourages people to celebrate and express themselves in a way that is unique to them.”

	BOTOX® Cosmetic continues to lead the aesthetics industry as the most requested product of its kind with 95% of specialists who would choose it and millions of patients treated, according to a July 2023 study*.

	*Based on a 2023 online survey of 120 healthcare providers.

	“BOTOX® Cosmetic is the most researched neurotoxin on the market*, so I trust it to deliver the precise, predictable results I want*,” Jensen says. “I’m thoughtful about what I put into and on my body, and I like knowing BOTOX® Cosmetic has been studied for decades. When treated by a licensed provider who is an expert in facial anatomy, the results are subtle. People in my life only notice I have less lines, but I still look like me. That’s exactly how I want to show up, like myself.”

	*Over 6,800 publications featuring BOTOX® (onabotulinumtoxinA) or BOTOX® Cosmetic.

	*In a 2024 online survey in which 250 neurotoxin patients from a base of neurotoxin users of the past 2 years with awareness of the BOTOX® Cosmetic brand were asked which of the attributes they associated with each brand, 82% (n = 231) stated that BOTOX® Cosmetic “Is a brand I trust.”



	

	



	The “One & Only” campaign salutes real people through presence, not perfection. Each face featured in the campaign reflects one-of-a-kind paths forged and brings out their originality. Their reasons for choosing BOTOX® Cosmetic are as personal as their reflections in the mirror.

	“At Allergan Aesthetics, we recognize that authenticity is paramount for today’s consumers — and it’s important to us too,” Curran says. “We want to showcase the people who use BOTOX® Cosmetic, which is what drove us to feature real, unique people in our advertising campaign. The premise of the ‘One & Only’ campaign is that BOTOX® Cosmetic is the one and only product of its kind FDA approved for over 20 years 3, just like each individual treated is their own one and only person! It’s real and relatable because it’s true. Seeing real people being treated with our products allows others to see themselves in the ads, fostering a genuine connection with the brand.”
	

	In a world that follows conventions and societal pressures, “One & Only” reminds audiences to stand out, not by being louder, but by being truer.

	As part of the upcoming “The Bold Pursuit” series, in partnership with PMC and Allergan Pharmaceutical Corp., Variety Content Studio will spotlight cinematographer Anna Mendes in an advertorial titled “The One & Only … Anna.” In addition to Variety, PMC oversees WWD and SHE Media.

	IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION BOTOX® Cosmetic may cause serious side effects that can be life threatening. Get medical help right away if you have any of these problems any time (hours to weeks) after injection of BOTOX® Cosmetic: 


Problems swallowing, speaking, or breathing, due to weakening of associated muscles, which can be severe and result in loss of life. You are at the highest risk if these problems are preexisting before injection. Swallowing problems may last for several months. 
Spread of toxin effects. The effect of botulinum toxin may affect areas away from the injection site and cause serious symptoms, including loss of strength and all-over muscle weakness, double vision, blurred vision and drooping eyelids, hoarseness or change or loss of voice, trouble saying words clearly, loss of bladder control, trouble breathing, and trouble swallowing. 



	BOTOX® Cosmetic dosing units are not the same as, or comparable to, any other botulinum toxin product. 

	There has not been a confirmed serious case of spread of toxin effect when BOTOX® Cosmetic has been used at the recommended dose to treat frown lines, crow’s feet lines, forehead lines, and/or platysma bands. 

	BOTOX® Cosmetic may cause loss of strength or general muscle weakness, vision problems, or dizziness within hours to weeks of receiving BOTOX® Cosmetic. If this happens, do not drive a car, operate machinery, or do other dangerous activities. 

	Serious and/or immediate allergic reactions have been reported, including itching, rash, red itchy welts, wheezing, asthma symptoms, or dizziness or feeling faint. Get medical help right away if you are wheezing or have asthma symptoms, or if you become dizzy or faint. 

	Do not receive BOTOX® Cosmetic if you are allergic to any of the ingredients in BOTOX® Cosmetic (see Medication Guide for ingredients); had an allergic reaction to any other botulinum toxin product such as Myobloc (rimabotulinumtoxinB), Dysport (abobotulinumtoxinA), Xeomin (incobotulinumtoxinA), Jeuveau (prabotulinumtoxinA-xvfs), Daxxify (daxibotulinumtoxinA-lanm), or Letybo (letibotulinumtoxinA-wlbg); or have a skin infection at the planned injection site. This list may not include all available botulinum toxin products. 

	Tell your doctor about all your muscle or nerve conditions, such as ALS or Lou Gehrig’s disease, myasthenia gravis, or Lambert-Eaton syndrome, as you may be at increased risk of serious side effects, including difficulty swallowing and difficulty breathing, from standard doses of BOTOX® Cosmetic. 
	

	Tell your doctor about all your medical conditions, including surgery or plans to have surgery on your face, trouble raising your eyebrows, drooping eyelids, any other abnormal facial change, are pregnant or plan to become pregnant (it is not known if BOTOX® Cosmetic can harm your unborn baby), or are breastfeeding or plan to (it is not known if BOTOX® Cosmetic passes into breast milk). 

	Tell your doctor about all the medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements. Using BOTOX® Cosmetic with certain other medicines may cause serious side effects. Do not start any new medicines until you have told your doctor that you have received BOTOX® Cosmetic in the past. 

	Tell your doctor if you have received any other botulinum toxin product in the last 4 months; have received injections of botulinum toxin such as Myobloc, Dysport, Xeomin, Jeuveau, Daxxify, or Letybo in the past (tell your doctor exactly which product you received); have recently received an antibiotic by injection; take muscle relaxants; take an allergy or cold medicine; take a sleep medicine; or take aspirin-like products or blood thinners. 

	Other side effects of BOTOX® Cosmetic include dry mouth; discomfort or pain at the injection site; tiredness; headache; neck pain; and eye problems, including double vision, blurred vision, decreased eyesight, drooping eyelids and eyebrows, swelling of eyelids, and dry eyes. 

	Approved Uses BOTOX® Cosmetic is a prescription medicine that is injected into muscles and used to temporarily improve the look of moderate to severe forehead lines, crow’s feet lines, frown lines between the eyebrows, and vertical bands connecting the jaw and neck (platysma bands) in adults. 

	For more information, refer to the Medication Guide or talk with your doctor.  

	To report a side effect, please call Allergan Aesthetics at 1-800-678-1605. 

	Please see BOTOX® Cosmetic full Prescribing Information including Boxed Warning and Medication Guide. 
	

	US-FA-SM-02447 11/26

title: How Netflix and the NFL Hope to Establish New Thanksgiving Eve Tradition With Game and U2 Half-Time Show: ‘We Want to Create Those Global Water Cooler Moments’
description: Thanksgiving Day has sported NFL games since the league’s inception in 1920, and now Turkey Day tussles on the gridiron are supercharged for the st
body:
Thanksgiving Day has sported NFL games since the league’s inception in 1920, and now Turkey Day tussles on the gridiron are supercharged for the streaming future.

	On Nov. 25, Netflix and the NFL would like football fans to join them for a new holiday tradition: the Thanksgiving Eve game. And like the streamer’s Christmas Day gridiron matchups, this one is A-list all the way: the Los Angeles Rams vs. the Green Bay Packers at L.A.’s SoFi Stadium and a halftime show headlined by U2.
	

	Gabe Spitzer, Netflix’s VP of global live sports and entertainment, says that cooking up a Thanksgiving Eve game came naturally between Netflix and the NFL. The partners have had great success in the last two years with Christmas Day games, with the matchups hitting 30 million-plus global viewers per game. The focus on showcasing games during holiday periods has conditioned Netflix subscribers and football fans to think of the streamer as a place for out-of-the-ordinary games.

	“As the NFL opened up more inventory and started talking to us about [possibly adding] more games, [Thanksgiving Eve] is one that they mentioned and immediately it felt like the perfect fit,” says Spitzer, who spoke with Variety while sporting a New England Patriots cap.

	Onnie Bose, the NFL’s VP of broadcasting, echoes that sentiment. The league has learned “over the last few years that when family and friends are together, they gravitate toward watching our games,” Bose says. “Our Thanksgiving viewership has always been strong. I think it’s exploded. We hit 57 million viewers with the Kansas City-Dallas game last year.”
	

	There is precedent for staking out new NFL-watching traditions, as the league has worked closely with Amazon Prime Video over the last few years to successfully establish the Black Friday game on the day after Thanksgiving.

	“We’ve been building Black Friday with Amazon over the last few years. So Thanksgiving is a clear natural weekend where people are together,” Bose says. “They’re watching football. We’ve seen that on Christmas also in the last few years. We just looked at it as an opportunity to do something new.”

	It’s been a fruitful marriage between the NFL, which has wants to expand the popularity of football around the world, and the streaming giant with its global footprint in 190 countries. For Thanksgiving Eve, NBC Sports is producing the game broadcast; EverWonder Studio is serving as executive producer for Netflix. Jesse Collins Entertainment, the banner known for handling the Emmy Awards, Oscars and Super Bowl Halftime show, is producing U2’s halftime performance.

	Netflix’s expanded agreement with the NFL runs through the 2029 season, with a growing presence across the NFL calendar, from Week 1 through Super Bowl week.

	This year, Netflix streamed the first-ever NFL game played in Australia, a matchup between the San Francisco 49ers and the Los Angeles Rams, on Sept. 10. The NFL also played games in London, Madrid, Munich, Rio de Janeiro, Paris and Mexico City this year. Live sports are a coveted draw for broadcasters and streamers alike. In the U.S., through the Nov. 22 matchup, the NFL has averaged 18.2 million viewers across its broadcasts, its highest mid-season number since 2010.

	Netflix’s partnership with the league includes Christmas Day games, the NFL’s first regular-season game in Australia, the Thanksgiving Eve game, a Week 18 matchup and the annual NFL Honors awards ceremony.

	This week’s game marks Netflix’s second time working with the L.A. Rams this season.

	“Our experience working with Netflix has been fantastic. There is a shared commitment between the Rams and Netflix to put fans first and deliver an exceptional experience, both inside SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, and for audiences watching around the globe,” says Kathryn Kai-ling Frederick, chief marketing officer for the Rams. “Netflix brings a unique ability to combine world-class storytelling, entertainment and live sports, creating opportunities to reach new audiences and elevate the way fans engage with the game. We’re excited to continue building on our relationship and collaborate on moments that extend beyond the field.”
	

	The strategy with the NFL is to create lasting moments and cement Netflix in the viewers’ minds as a marquee destination for top games and entertainment. “We’re not the networks that have hundreds of games a year. We’re really showing up intentionally at a few points across the season, and I think this is where Thanksgiving Eve fits in perfectly,” Spitzer says. “We’re that opening game, an international game in Melbourne, Thanksgiving Eve, two games on Christmas and then that final weekend of the season when stakes are all on the line for some of these potential playoff teams.”

	The Rams and Packers, both with a record of 6-4, are each fighting for a spot in the playoffs, which means that Wednesday’s game has big consequences for both teams’ seasons.

	Bose says that the Netflix partnership was a natural for the NFL’s plans, especially after seeing how the streamer brought the spotlight to its Christmas Day games.

	“They’ve truly embraced Christmas. They’ve made it into a big event with their double headers. It’s worldwide distribution. They’ve engaged in putting on concerts,” Bose says. “There’s not a lot of places where we can add new windows where we have partners that are well established in certain places. This was a new window. It fits with their strategy of wanting to have kind of events and standalone windows that resonate.”

	Spitzer says that Netflix approaches its live events with an eye to setting a high bar in the pop culture landscape. It did that in 2024 with the “Beyoncé Bowl” during the Houston Texans-Baltimore Ravens Christmas Day game, which drew some 27 million viewers in the U.S., not to mention the social media conversation generated by her performance. Beyonce’s revue included Shaboozey, the Texas Southern University’s Oceans of Soul Marching band and a wide range of performers that spoke to Southern Black and Latin history and music.

	In 2025, Snoop Dogg’s halftime show for Netflix’s Christmas Day games drew 29 million viewers and featured country superstar Lainey Wilson and the hitmakers of “K-pop Demon Hunters”: EJAE, Audrey Nuna and Rei Ami.

	“Obviously, we’re so early in our live sports journey, but it was a great start,” Spitzer says.

	With U2, Netflix aims to create another big moment with a band that’s a household name worldwide. “They’ve only done it twice,” Spitzer says about the rock superstars’ NFL game appearances. U2 played in the 2002 game in a moving set that was also a tribute to the victims of 9/11; the other was as an opening act on “Monday Night Football” in 2006 as part of the reopening of the Louisiana Superdome a year after the devastation of Hurricane Katrina. “They want to be a part of a big moment, and we’re thrilled that they want to be on Netflix for launching this new tradition as well,” Spitzer says.
	

	The streamer is also bringing celebrity chef David Chang aboard in the pregame show to spotlight food, tailgating and other game-day traditions. For Netflix, it’s as much of a live event strategy as it is a sports strategy.

	“It’s about creating that new fandom. We want to create those global water cooler moments,” says Spitzer. “That could be a big boxing match. It could be NFL games. It could be the Women’s World Cup, or it could be Alex Honnold climbing a 101-story building. If we’re going to do a big live event, we really want to make sure it cuts through.”

	Netflix has the rights to the 2027 and 2031 FIFA Women’s World Cup, so lessons learned staging NFL games and other live events look to culminate next year in Brazil. Spitzer won’t comment on whether the streamer is bidding for the 2030 and 2024 Men’s World Cup rights.

	The Women’s World Cup is “the most ambitious project that we’ve ever done. Thirty straight days, 64 matches over eight hours a day in the U.S. and Canada,” Spitzer says. “We’ve been planning it for two years. There’s nothing bigger, so we can’t wait for that.”

	For Netflix, aligning with the biggest brand in U.S. sports — the NFL — and creating a new tradition is good for driving global subscriptions and good for the bottom line in a business that has seen layoffs and management shake-ups like every other content giant. For the next few weeks, Team Netflix is all about driving viewership to Thanksgiving Eve and Christmas Day action on the gridiron.

	“We want to create a new family tradition with Netflix,” Spitzer says. “It’s really about bringing fans together for the biggest moments in sports.”

schema.headline: How Netflix and the NFL Hope to Establish New Thanksgiving Eve Tradition With Game and U2 Half-Time Show: ‘We Want to Create Those Global Water Cooler Moments’

title: MS NOW Hosts ‘Disappointed’ Management Has Yet to Reach New WGA Union Deal Guaranteeing ‘Fair Wages’; Network Boss Rebecca Kutler Responds to Accusations
description: Rachel Maddow and more than a dozen other MS NOW on-air hosts issued a public letter urging parent company Versant Media to reach a new deal with u
body:
Rachel Maddow and more than a dozen other MS NOW on-air hosts issued a public letter urging parent company Versant Media to reach a new deal with unionized employees affiliated with WGA East that ensures “fair wages and protections,” before their previous agreement expires Dec. 3.

	Rebecca Kutler, MS NOW’s president, responded to their complaints in a memo to the outlet’s staffers — writing in part, “We must weigh every financial commitment against our ability to invest in journalism.”
	

	Writers Guild of America East members at MS NOW are currently negotiating for a second collective bargaining agreement. “Despite the network’s historic midterm ratings and strong performance across the business, workers are still fighting for a fair contract with Versant Media Group management,” the union said.

	MS NOW hosts and guests including Rachel Maddow, Jen Psaki, Christopher Hayes, Lawrence O’Donnell and Nicolle Wallace signed onto “a letter of solidarity calling for a fair wages and protections for the MS NOW Union,” released Tuesday by WGA East. Others signing the letter included Ali Velshi, Amy McGrath, Alicia Menendez, Jacob Soboroff, David Noriega, Jillian Frankel, Ayman Mohyeldin, Katie Phang, Christine Jansing, Symone Sanders Townsend, Antonia Hylton, Jonathan Capehart and Michael Steele. (The signatories to the letter are not covered by the WGAE agreement.)

	The letter, which WGA East said was delivered to Versant management at the bargaining table, reads: “As hosts and guests of MS NOW programs, we stand in solidarity with the MS NOW Union as they fight for a contract that addresses inflation, AI protections and retirement security. As one of the most trusted names in news, we are proud of our programming and the MS NOW producers that make it possible. We’re disappointed that Versant Media’s decision makers expect unit members to work extra hours creating new digital content, without treating it as extra work or paying for it. On top of that, we are disappointed that Versant Media will not agree to the Union’s demands for annual and minimum wage increases that keep pace with inflation. We are calling on the company to agree to a quick and fair process to recognize all employees’ rightful place in the MS NOW Union without division or delay. Additionally, we call on the company to agree to a contract that will protect wages, benefits and security at work.”
	

	Kutler, who has led MS NOW since January 2025, addressed many of the allegations in a memo. “Let me be clear: we support our employees’ right to organize, to be represented, and to advocate for themselves. That has never been in question, nor should it be,” she wrote.

	According to Kutler, MS NOW has already reached “tentative agreements” with WGAE on “numerous issues throughout this process and shown a willingness to find common ground where differences remain.” 

	“We have made meaningful proposals to increase compensation, address workload concerns, expand opportunities for growth and advancement, and provide protections against AI, among many other offerings,” Kutler said. 

	That said, according to Kutler, MS NOW’s success “does not insulate us from the financial pressures reshaping our industry. It takes a realistic understanding of these market pressures for us to continue our success. We must weigh every financial commitment against our ability to invest in journalism, develop new programming, hire journalists, cover the 2028 presidential campaign, and build out platforms that will carry MS NOW into the future, including our direct-to-consumer offering.”

	Kutler said MS NOW will “continue to compensate our employees fairly and competitively, while protecting our long-term growth. Those responsibilities are not mutually exclusive, but they require thoughtful decisions.” 

	“As we approach the final weeks of these negotiations, let’s stay focused on what unites us: our shared commitment to the journalism we produce, the audiences who count on us, and the future of MS NOW. I am optimistic that together we will reach a fair and responsible agreement that reflects the respect we have for our colleagues and the work we do together,” Kutler said.

	In addition to guarantees on wages and overtime pay for MS NOW union workers, the WGAE is seeking to expand union jurisdiction at MS NOW during negotiations for the unit’s second union contract. The currently 300-member bargaining unit is demanding union recognition for approximately 50 additional workers including employees in MS NOW’s digital, audio and longform, newsgathering, planning and DC bureau divisions.

	The union’s first contract, ratified as the MSNBC Union in 2023, included a minimum 3% pay increase every year for the three-year contract’s duration and improvements to policies regarding extra pay for additional work, overnight work and out-of-title work.
	

	MS NOW changed its name from MSNBC in the fall of 2025, ahead of its spin-off as part of Versant from NBCUniversal at the beginning of this year.

	In the past year, Kutler noted in her memo Tuesday, MS NOW reached new collective bargaining agreements with other labor organizations, including two International Alliance of Theatrical Stage Employees locals and the Directors Guild of America.

	According to Kutler, MS NOW offers the highest starting salaries among its peers, “having raised entry-level salaries significantly over the last five years, and the starting point for each role’s salary range is typically higher than our broadcast and cable news competitors.” In addition, according to Kutler, “while many other news organizations are cutting back their newsrooms and trimming roles, we have filled more than 200 in the past year at MS NOW and continue recruiting for dozens of open positions.”

title: Anthropic and OpenAI Staff Worried Models Becoming Too Powerful to Ever Release, Report
description:
Anthropic & OpenAI
                          Staff Fears Models Too Powerful To Ever Release
body:
Anthropic & OpenAI
                          Staff Fears Models Too Powerful To Ever Release
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 24, 2026
                            9:03 AM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              Employees at two major artificial intelligence companies are concerned about the powerful new models being cooked up in the lab ... which some believe should never be released to the public.
      
    
              Axios says its reporters have spoken to more than two dozen sources familiar with the internal debate over the new models at Anthropic and OpenAI ... and they've told the outlet there are stronger versions of A.I. than the ones currently available for public consumption.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
              While the companies have worked to make them safe enough to release to the world, they've been unable to do so ... and there's a concern that these models are too smart -- and they're struggling to control them in internal testing environments.
      

              There are two major issues, according to Axios ... the first is that because A.I. is incentivized by a rewards-based system, there's concern that it will cheat and break parameters to gain the maximum reward.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
              The second concern is that A.I. knows researchers are now watching it ... and these models aren't necessarily showing their work to the researchers anymore -- making it impossible to know what the A.I. is thinking.
      
    
              Multiple sources Axios spoke to said they feel some top-level executives have become out of touch with the serious safety risks.
      
    
              It's unclear where the companies go from here ... but, bottom line, industry leaders are seriously concerned.
